verdict.rationale: Cognee's session/caching model explicitly stores ordered per-session interactions keyed by (user_id, session_id), and `.recall()` retrieves relevant memory while `.improve()` is documented specifically for use 'at the end of a chat or agent session to bridge short-term session memory into permanent memory,' enabling an agent to pick up context from a prior session. However, the docs describe storing/retrieving raw interaction history and enriching the graph rather than an explicit 'summary' generation feature, and there's no independent/hands-on confirmation of this exact workflow. Missing for 10: documented explicit session-summary output format, third-party validation that agents actually resume threads using this mechanism.
